subject: history
title: Life & thought in the Greek world

lesson.opening: What social arrangements supported Greek intellectual and artistic life?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Citizenship, households, and slavery

Theater, philosophy, and civic life

Hellenistic centers of learning

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: A useful account links ideas to schools, patrons, households, public festivals, and political settings. Cultural influence and political independence do not rise and fall together.

sections.heading: Keep the question
sections.body: What social arrangements supported Greek intellectual and artistic life?

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “Parthenon construction begins” or “Foundation of Alexandria”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.

activities.prompt: “Political conquest necessarily ends the influence of a culture.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: The influence of Greek language, education, and art under Roman rule provides a way to test and challenge this claim.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
Connect one artistic or intellectual practice to the institution that supported it.
